raw_response:
I will mostly do what works here and adjust a little. I only farmed one year myself, so I will not make big changes. Around here, wheat-maize is the steady way, and with a well I do not have to depend only on rain. I will keep most of my land in wheat and then summer maize on the same ground, because that is the safer income. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, not too much, because cotton needs more watching and more spraying. On wheat land, I will use a bit more fertilizer rather than risk thin seedlings and low heads. On maize, I will feed it enough nitrogen because if maize is hungry, yield drops fast. Cotton I will not plant too wide this year; I will keep it on a smaller area and give it fewer inputs than maize-wheat, but still enough so it does not fall behind. My farm is 10.1 mu and only 2 people work it, so I will keep the work simple: rotary tillage where I can, improved or hybrid seed where people nearby had decent results, 2 to 4 irrigations depending on the crop, and regular pesticide sprays when insects or disease show up. I care about cost, but I fear losing yield more than spending a few more yuan on fertilizer.
